item.title: Overview of Awesome LLM Causal Reasoning Works and Methods
item.description:
Overview of Awesome LLM Causal Reasoning Works and Methods

Awesome LLM Causal Reasoning is a collection of LLM-based causal reasoning works, including papers, codes, and datasets, providing a comprehensive review of research aimed at enhancing Large Language Models for causal reasoning (CR).

🧩 How it works

  • Existing methods are categorized based on the role of LLMs: either as reasoning engines or as helpers providing knowledge or data to traditional CR methods.
  • End tasks are categorized into three groups: causal discovery, causal inference, and additional causal tasks.
  • Performance of LLMs is evaluated on various causal reasoning tasks using pass@1 accuracy with strategies such as zero-shot.

⚙️ Key details

The collection includes various notable works and papers:

item.title: Algebraic Characterization of Two-Block Shallow ReLU Pattern Varieties
item.description:
Algebraic Characterization of Two-Block Shallow ReLU Pattern Varieties

A complete algebraic characterization of two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties has been submitted on 18 Nov 2026.

🔍 Overview

  • Submitted on 18 Nov 2026 under the title “Defining equations for two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties”.
  • Proves a conjecture of Alexandr-Montúfar.

⚙️ Key details

  • The research gives a complete algebraic characterization of two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties.
  • Researchers show that determinantal equations arising from rank constraints imposed by the activation patterns generate the defining ideals.
  • The set-theoretic proof utilizes a characterization of orbit closures of matrix pencils in terms of the Kronecker canonical form.

#ReLU #NeuralNetworks #Mathematics #MachineLearning #Research

Source: Defining equations for two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties

item.title: Researchers Explore Steering Mixture-of-Experts Models with Targeted Expert Paths
item.description:
Researchers Explore Steering Mixture-of-Experts Models with Targeted Expert Paths

Researchers have investigated how forcing tokens onto chosen expert paths influences the behavior of mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models. The approach involves building a target path from the experts that a concept’s or role’s tokens most often use, and adding a fixed bias to each target expert’s router logit during generation to steer the token toward this expert path.

Two kinds of targets are studied:

  • Format targets concern the form of the output.
  • Concept targets concern its topic.

In Qwen3-30B-A3B, steering a format path changes the text the model writes. Steering a concept path shifts the model’s next-token probabilities toward the concept, even when the path is built in another language, yet this shift has little effect on the generated text.

The researchers investigate why formats reach the text but concepts do not by steering only part of the generation, and find evidence that a format, once started, reinforces itself. They show that the concepts religion and money steer most strongly, and that the effect is concentrated in the middle layers. An analysis of embedding distinctiveness and word frequency is attempted to explain why the strength of the effect varies by concept.

#AI #LanguageModels #MixtureofExperts #Research #Steering

Source: What MoE Routing Controls: Causal Interventions on Expert Trajectories

item.title: New MCP Servers Extend AI Capabilities
item.description:
New MCP Servers Extend AI Capabilities

A collection of MCP servers has been introduced, extending AI capabilities through various integrations.

🔍 Overview

  • MCP is an open protocol enabling AI models to interact with local and remote resources.
  • This list focuses on production-ready and experimental MCP servers.
  • Servers extend AI capabilities through file access, database connections, API integrations, and other contextual services.

🧩 How it works

  • MCP servers allow AI models to securely interact with resources.
  • Servers can be installed and run from GitHub repositories.
  • A web-based directory is available, synced with the repository.

⚙️ Key details

  • Servers for accessing many apps and tools through a single MCP server.
  • Automatically fetches the latest arXiv papers on VLN, VLA, SLAM, 3D, and Embodied AI.
  • Each section in the README corresponds to a search keyword.
  • The full list of papers is available in the papers/ directory.

🚀 Availability

  • Servers are available for installation and running from GitHub repositories.
  • A web-based directory is synced with the repository.

💡 Why it matters

  • Extends AI capabilities through various integrations.
  • Automatically fetches the latest research papers.
  • Provides a centralized directory for MCP servers.

📚 References

  • Checkout awesome-mcp-clients and glama.ai/mcp/clients.
  • Looking for a hosted server? See awesome-remote-mcp-servers.
  • Embodied-AI-Daily Web: http://luohongkun.top/Embodied-AI-Daily/

item.title: UNESCO and ENS Launch AI Ethics Call for Early‑Career Researchers
item.description:
UNESCO and ENS Launch AI Ethics Call for Early‑Career Researchers

UNESCO and the AI and Society Institute at École normale supérieure (ENS‑PSL) have opened a call for papers inviting researchers who earned their PhD within the last five years to submit proposals on the ethics of artificial intelligence.

🔍 Overview

  • The initiative follows UNESCO’s 2021 Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence.
  • It aims to promote emerging research, foster interdisciplinary exchange, and link scholarship with public policy and practice.

📅 Key Details

  • Selected proposals will be invited to present at a one‑day academic event in Paris on 10 December 2026.
  • The event will gather emerging scholars, established researchers, and institutional representatives for thematic discussions and expert feedback.
  • General participation is open to everyone; registration will be available on UNESCO’s website.

🎓 Eligibility

  • Researchers who completed a PhD within the past five years.
  • Work must address issues related to AI ethics.
  • Applications are welcomed from all disciplines and geographic regions.
  • Interdisciplinary, cross‑sectoral, theoretical, empirical, comparative, and practice‑oriented contributions are encouraged.
  • Co‑authored proposals are allowed if all authors meet the eligibility criteria.

📝 Submission Guidelines

  • Submit an extended abstract of 800–1,000 words (references excluded) in English, in Word or PDF format.
  • Abstracts must be anonymized (no author names or identifying information).
  • Proposals will be reviewed by laureates and jury members of the UNESCO Beruniy Prize for Scientific Research on the Ethics of AI.
  • Successful applicants will be notified by 15 November 2026 and asked to deliver a full paper of 5,000–7,000 words by 1 December 2026.

✈️ Travel Support

  • One selected author will receive travel support to attend the Paris event, alongside members of the UNESCO Beruniy Prize International Jury and Laureates.

📚 Post‑Event Opportunities

  • Proceedings will be compiled by UNESCO and the AI and Society Institute.
  • Selected authors may adapt their research for publication in the Tribune of the Conseil de l’intelligence artificielle et du numérique (CIANum), reaching a broader public and policy audience.

#UNESCO #AIethics #CallForPapers #Research

Source: Call for papers: Advancing research on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

item.title: SurfSense Launches as Open-Source Research Platform for AI Agents
item.description:
SurfSense Launches as Open-Source Research Platform for AI Agents

SurfSense has launched as an open-source, self-hostable alternative to NotebookLM, designed specifically as a research platform for AI agents. It provides a framework for agents to perform live web research, turning findings into structured briefs and alerts.

🔍 Overview

SurfSense functions as an agent harness that manages the infrastructure for web research, including retries, structured output, and credit metering. It allows users to go from a question to a cited brief without building custom plumbing.

🧩 How it works

Agents access live data through a single REST API or an MCP server. The platform exposes every connector as a native tool, compatible with Claude, Cursor, and other agent frameworks. It also supports external MCP connectors for integration with services like Notion, Slack, and Jira.

⚙️ Key details

Platform Data Provided
Reddit Posts, comments, subreddit streams
YouTube Videos, transcripts, comment threads
Instagram Public profiles, posts, reels
TikTok Videos, comments, hashtags, profiles
Google Maps Places, ratings, reviews
Google Search Live SERPs
Indeed Public job postings, salaries, descriptions
Amazon Prices, ratings, offers, sellers, best-seller ranks
Walmart Product data, full review history, prices, variants
Web Crawl Clean, structured content from any web page

🚀 Availability

SurfSense is available as an open-source and self-hosted solution. The platform includes a built-in knowledge base that keeps findings searchable with citations, supporting features such as chat, reports, podcasts, presentations, and automations.

#AI #OpenSource #Research #WebAutomation

Source: MODSetter/SurfSense

item.title: UWA Launches Researcher Development Academy to Support University Research
item.description:
UWA Launches Researcher Development Academy to Support University Research

The University of Western Australia (UWA) has launched the Researcher Development Academy (RDA), a university-wide initiative designed to integrate researcher training, leadership development, and industry engagement under a single framework.

🔍 Overview

Launched by Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Science and Innovation, Yaz Muburakai MLA, the academy aims to strengthen research excellence and societal impact. It serves over 4,000 researchers, including higher degree by research (HDR) students, early-to-mid-career researchers, senior researchers, and supervisors.

⚙️ Key Details

The academy provides an integrated framework focused on research capability, leadership, communication, and career development. Key focus areas include:

  • Training in entrepreneurial mindsets and commercialization pipelines.
  • Project management and collaborative teamwork skills.
  • Communicating research to diverse audiences.

🧩 Programs and Activities

Program/Activity Description
Research Ready Integrated training and support framework
Future Forward Professional and leadership development
HDR Supervisor Training Training for research supervisors
Bold Ideas, Better Futures Flagship series featuring industry and academic speakers

💡 Why it matters

According to Pro Vice-Chancellor (Research Training), Professor Hélène de Burgh-Woodman, the academy is a significant investment in researchers and aligns with State priorities in innovation, workforce development, and economic diversification. The academy recently hosted its first theme, “Research Futures in the Age of AI,” which explored artificial intelligence in higher education, including an international keynote by Professor James Zou from Stanford University on AI agents and scientific discovery.

#UWA #Research #HigherEducation #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: New Researcher Development Academy to strengthen WA’s future workforce

item.title: Dude: Dual-Detection Multi-Agent System for Paper-Code Discrepancy Detection
item.description:
Dude: Dual-Detection Multi-Agent System for Paper-Code Discrepancy Detection

LLM‑empowered paper‑code discrepancy detection has received growing concern because the scaling of research submissions exceeds the manual review capability. In this paper, the authors propose Dude, the first Dual‑Detection Multi‑Agent System for paper‑code discrepancy detection.

🔍 Overview

  • LLM‑empowered paper‑code discrepancy detection is under growing concern as submission volume outpaces manual review.
  • Dude is presented as the first Dual‑Detection Multi‑Agent System targeting this problem.

🛠️ How it works

  • The system tackles granularity asymmetry between paper‑language and code‑language, which introduces over‑interpretation and over‑reporting challenges that increase false positives.
  • Two mechanisms are introduced to prevent false reporting:
Component Purpose
Granularity‑aligned negotiation Aligns the granularity of paper‑language and code‑language to avoid over‑interpretation
Two‑stage salience‑filtering Filters salient information to stop agents from falsely reporting discrepancies

📈 Results

  • Experimental results on real‑world paper‑code discrepancy datasets show Dude improves recall and precision by up to 22.8 % and raises the F1 score by up to 18.7 % compared to baseline methods.

💡 Why it matters

  • By reducing false positives and improving detection accuracy, Dude helps alleviate the manual workload caused by the scaling of research submissions.

#papercode #AIagents #discrepancydetection #LLM #research

Source: Dude: A Dual-Detection Multi-Agent System for Paper-Code Discrepancy Detection
